before_taxonomy.classification_basis: Cruise's initial mandatory crash reports omitted the materially relevant post-crash dragging behaviour. The required regulatory reporting artefact therefore presented a truncated account of the captured occurrence, degrading audit-evidence integrity before NHTSA review. The post-crash dragging event was captured in other evidence and was later identifiable; the failure was its omission from the required regulatory report rather than complete non-capture of the event. NHTSA was ultimately able to reconstruct the omitted dragging behaviour sufficiently to make a regulatory finding, so the audit trail was not rendered non-reconstructable.

evidence_search.notes: Current screen reads the repository-preserved source-attributed evidence and complete episode inventory. It does not claim fresh full-text access to every originating source. No canonical restamp or independent source verification is implied.

episode_inventory.purpose: Preserve the source-language or evidentiary propositions that materially explain VIGIL's governance interpretation. Paraphrases are concise, source-bounded and linked to the existing taxonomy adjudication.

clauses.source_paraphrase: On 2 October 2023, following an initial collision involving a pedestrian and a human-driven vehicle, the driverless Cruise vehicle moved after impact and dragged the pedestrian approximately 20 feet before stopping. The available record does not establish the Cruise system's internal perception or intent.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: The Cruise vehicle's post-collision movement was a distinct safety mechanism from the initial impact and from the later reporting omission. The evidence establishes the movement and dragging outcome but not the vehicle's internal perception, planning state or intent.

clauses.source_paraphrase: After the 2 October 2023 crash, two required Cruise crash reports omitted the post-crash dragging behaviour. NHTSA later identified the omission after reviewing requested crash video, and announced a consent order on 30 September 2024.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: A required regulatory report must preserve all materially relevant captured event state through selection and summarisation so the regulator can assess the actual safety occurrence.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: Omitting the post-impact movement produced a truncated audit artefact before NHTSA review, even though that behaviour was central to the vehicle's separate safety consequence.

The post-crash dragging event was captured in other evidence and was later identifiable; the failure was its omission from the required regulatory report rather than complete non-capture of the event.
NHTSA was ultimately able to reconstruct the omitted dragging behaviour sufficiently to make a regulatory finding, so the audit trail was not rendered non-reconstructable.
